KB-1042.title: API Gateway timeout troubleshooting guide
KB-1042.problem: Customer-facing API endpoints return 502 Bad Gateway or 504 Gateway Timeout errors when the API Gateway cannot reach healthy upstream services within the configured timeout threshold.
symptoms: Upstream connect timeout messages in API Gateway logs
P99 latency exceeding 4 seconds on affected routes
Circuit breaker OPEN state for upstream services
KB-1042.rootCause: Upstream service unavailability or slow response caused by connection pool exhaustion, deployment regressions, or misconfigured health checks. The gateway times out waiting for a response from the upstream before the client connection is closed.

resolutionSteps.title: Confirm upstream health
resolutionSteps.description: Check upstream service health endpoints and pod readiness. Verify no deployment in progress.

resolutionSteps.title: Review gateway error logs
resolutionSteps.description: Search for upstream timed out and connection refused messages. Correlate timestamps with deployment events.

resolutionSteps.title: Check connection pool metrics
resolutionSteps.description: Inspect HikariCP active/waiting connection counts on upstream services. Pool exhaustion is the most common root cause.

resolutionSteps.title: Apply interim mitigation
resolutionSteps.description: Enable circuit breaker, increase pool size, or route traffic to secondary region while investigating.

resolutionSteps.title: Execute rollback if needed
resolutionSteps.description: If error spike correlates with a recent deployment, follow the rollback runbook KB-0891.

resolutionSteps.title: Validate recovery
resolutionSteps.description: Confirm error rate returns to baseline and P99 latency is below 2 seconds for 15 minutes.

commands.label: Check gateway pod status
commands.description: Verify all gateway pods are Running and ready.

commands.label: Tail gateway error logs
commands.command: kubectl logs -n production -l app=api-gateway --tail=100 | grep -E 'ERROR|upstream timed out'
commands.description: Filter for upstream timeout and 502 errors.

commands.label: Connection pool metrics
commands.description: Check active connection count against pool maximum.

aiSummary.summary: This runbook addresses 502/504 gateway errors caused by upstream unavailability. The most effective resolution path is verifying upstream health, checking connection pool metrics, and rolling back recent deployments if a regression is confirmed.
keyPoints: Connection pool exhaustion is the leading cause in 68% of similar incidents
Rollback resolves 94% of deployment-related timeout incidents within 20 minutes
Always validate recovery metrics for 15 minutes before closing the incident

KB-0891.title: Deployment rollback procedure — Core Banking
KB-0891.problem: A production deployment introduces regressions requiring immediate rollback to the previous stable version.
symptoms: Health checks failing on new pods
KB-0891.rootCause: Deployment regression — configuration or code change in the new version causes service degradation.

resolutionSteps.title: Approve rollback
resolutionSteps.description: Obtain team lead approval for production rollback.

resolutionSteps.title: Execute rollback
resolutionSteps.description: Run rollback command to revert to previous revision.

resolutionSteps.title: Validate
resolutionSteps.description: Confirm error rate returns to baseline.

aiSummary.summary: Standard rollback procedure for core-banking-svc production deployments with approval gates and validation steps.
